scope: Three groups of three P1 items: tool recovery/web/watchdogs; scheduling/fairness/delegation; messaging/timing/diagnostics. Product and benefit acceptance stay separate.

observed: Malformed or unregistered tool inputs receive bounded corrective handling. Repetitive stream output retains the partial reply and stops before a late tool call executes.
remaining: Current compiled-client presentation and the complete cross-provider malformed-input matrix remain open.

observed: Web fixtures retain backend wire contracts, reauthorize redirects, hide search credentials/provider bodies, bound content and cancel an in-flight response.
remaining: Live search relevance/recall and paid cost comparisons require the task baseline and budget; distinct backend result shapes are not treated as equivalent recall.

observed: The actual native-process watchdog test bounds headers, silence and pings without refilling the retry budget. Stale execution IDs cannot cancel a newer run. Worker tests bound spawn/frames/writes and reap stalled children.
remaining: A current-client wait-reason display and the full tool/approval/backpressure/MCP/LSP/subagent cancellation matrix are not established by these selected tests.

observed: Cron and wakeup store occurrence, expiry, ownership and timezone facts; fixtures cover distinct admissions, backlog coalescing, restart/fork behavior, cancellation and shared capacity. Timers create advisory wakes rather than directly running a model.
remaining: Current-client next-execution/timezone/expiry presentation and edit flows remain unverified. Timer execution cost belongs in the paid task/usage acceptance, not inferred from scheduler tests.

observed: Runtime admission uses bounded execution, job and subagent semaphores; independent Session operation and bounded scheduler capacity have fixture coverage.
remaining: Fleet-wide provider/terminal/LSP observability and queue/starvation/RSS/FD curves under sustained concurrent load are not supplied. Per-engine limits do not establish cross-Location fairness.

observed: Native delegation requires subagent authority, leaf-child constraints and bounded work. Tests cover durable background completion, archived references, denied delegation, leaf recursion refusal and turn-budget closure. Background-job recovery preserves unknown outcomes without restarting untracked work.
remaining: The complete current-client foreground-to-background, independent cancellation and parent-cancellation terminal-state matrix still needs acceptance.

observed: The shared peer tool rejects self/cross-project sends, checks message permission, bounds pending input and only wakes active peers by default. The local peer/background suites pass 19 tests with 77 assertions.
remaining: The send-message input/output has no explicit reply-to or admitted message receipt ID. Admission currently creates a fresh SessionMessage.ID, so this boundary alone does not prove restart/retry delivery deduplication. A persisted reply-loop cost budget and visible stop contract remain to be defined and tested.

observed: The native timing table retains locally measured TTFT and turn duration. Usage receipts retain run/step identity and auxiliary timing rather than inventing vendor telemetry.
remaining: A complete admission/queue/provider/tool/approval/summary/verification phase breakdown and expandable current wait-object presentation are not established. Existing TTFT/turn duration is not that complete breakdown.

observed: Native doctor is read-only, works during active ownership and reports version/platform/sandbox/supported transports and database integrity without claiming network or credential validity. The product doctor also analyzes resource/CPU trends.
remaining: A complete active-route/dependency diagnosis, redacted diagnostic export contract and bounded idle-overhead measurement remain open. Supported transport names are not proof of active-route health.
